question:
We have a DBT snapshot which runs daily and checks for the columns to expire existing data and then insert the latest data to snapshot table. Since the snapshot runs daily, data is growing exponentially in snapshot table and we want to limit the historical changes based on subset of columns and at the same time capture the latest data from dbt model to snapshot.

Consider below example

column1 column2 column3 column4 dbt_valid_from dbt_valid_to
A B C D 2023-06-01 2023-06-02
A B X D 2023-06-02 2023-06-03
A Y X D 2023-06-03 2023-06-04
A Z X D 2023-06-04 null

column2 and column3 are check columns in config block as shown below

 {{
    config(
      target_schema='snapshots',
      strategy='check',
      unique_key='column1',
      check_cols=['column2', 'column3'],
    )
}}

Now snapshots are working as expected. Our requirement is to check the columns column2 and column3 and update the snapshot regularly but skip capturing the history on column2 changes because data in column2 is changing very frequently and due to this the table volume is growing and the downstream applications are facing challenges to retrieve data from this snapshot table. If any changes in column3 we need to capture the history of these changes because downstream applications want this information.

Output should look something like this

on 2023-06-03 the data in snapshot should be like

column1 column2 column3 column4 dbt_valid_from dbt_valid_to
A B C D 2023-06-01 2023-06-02
A B X D 2023-06-02 2023-06-03
A Y X D 2023-06-03 null

on 2023-06-04 the data in snapshot should be like

column1 column2 column3 column4 dbt_valid_from dbt_valid_to
A B C D 2023-06-01 2023-06-02
A B X D 2023-06-02 2023-06-03
A Z X D 2023-06-03 null

so ideally if there is any change on column2 we should have latest data captured from model but it should not contain snapshot history. Is there a way to achieve this using dbt snapshot.
title: Capturing limited historical data in dbt snapshot
answer:
To implement your requirement where you want to capture changes for column3 but only update the latest data for column2 without maintaining its historical changes in a dbt snapshot, we can use a post-hook to adjust the behavior of the snapshot. Here's how you can structure your dbt snapshot configuration and include a post-hook to handle column2. Something like this might help:

{{
    config(
        target_schema='snapshots',
        strategy='check',
        unique_key='column1',
        check_cols=['column3'],  -- Only track historical changes for column3
        post_hook=[
            "UPDATE {{ this }} AS snp SET column2 = source_data.column2
            FROM {{ ref('your_source_model') }} AS source_data
            WHERE snp.column1 = source_data.column1
              AND snp.column2 <> source_data.column2
              AND snp.dbt_valid_to IS NULL"
        ]
    )
}}
